rationale: The workflow already applies dependency caching (Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 in every build/test job) and deliberately sets fail-fast: false on all matrix jobs to preserve full failure diagnostics, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is already in place and P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated (every matrix outcome is required). The only non-synthetic, measured evidence is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508), which bound a small Node.js checks job with timeout-minutes: 5. This repository's jobs are Rust build/test jobs—including release-mode property tests with 200000 cases and container builds in Alpine/FreeBSD—with no per-job duration data in ci_history, so I cannot verify the precondition of representative successful-duration history or exclude the contraindication that valid slow runs exceed a proposed limit. Introducing arbitrary timeout-minutes values risks killing valid runs and reducing build/test coverage. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated because the workflow contains publish-wiki and publish-docs deployment jobs. The remaining evidence records are explicitly synthetic scenario replays ('timings are scenario resource costs, not original repository CI savings') and do not establish repository savings. No suitable, safely-supported optimization is available for this workflow.
